content: 1. Men are recommended to follow a specific order of treatment preferences for cryptococcal meningitis. The first option is a short course of Amphotericin B (5–7 days) combined with high-dose fluconazole to complete a 2-week induction phase. This is advised when it is not feasible to provide pre-emptive hydration, electrolyte replacement, and toxicity monitoring for the full 2-week period. This recommendation is conditional and based on low-quality evidence. 2. If Amphotericin B is unavailable, the next option is high-dose fluconazole combined with flucytosine. This is also a conditional recommendation supported by low-quality evidence. 3. If neither Amphotericin B nor flucytosine is available, high-dose fluconazole alone is recommended. This is a conditional recommendation with low-quality evidence. 4. For the consolidation phase of treatment in HIV-infected adults, adolescents, and children with cryptococcal meningitis or disseminated non-meningeal disease, an 8-week antifungal regimen is recommended. This involves fluconazole at a dose of 400–800 mg/day following a 2-week induction phase with Amphotericin B (6–12 mg/kg/day, up to 400–800 mg/day for those under 19 years). 5. For patients treated with a short course of Amphotericin B or fluconazole-based induction therapy, fluconazole at 800 mg/day (or 12 mg/kg/day up to 800 mg/day for those under 19 years) is recommended for the consolidation phase. This is a strong recommendation based on low-quality evidence. 6. For maintenance treatment of cryptococcal disease in HIV-infected adults, adolescents, and children, oral fluconazole at 200 mg daily (or 6 mg/kg/day up to 200 mg/day for those under 19 years) is strongly recommended. This recommendation is supported by high-quality evidence. 7. For localized non-meningeal cryptococcal disease or isolated serum cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) positivity (where active cryptococcal meningitis has been excluded), fluconazole at 800 mg/day (or 12 mg/kg/day for those under 19 years) for 2 weeks, followed by 400 mg/day (or 6 mg/kg/day up to 400–800 mg/day for those under 19 years) for 8 weeks, and continued maintenance with fluconazole at 200 mg/day is recommended. The optimal antifungal regimen for this population remains undetermined, and this is a conditional recommendation based on low-quality evidence. 8. In HIV-infected adults receiving Amphotericin B-containing regimens for cryptococcal disease, a minimum package of toxicity prevention, monitoring, and management is strongly recommended to minimize serious Amphotericin B-related toxicities such as hypokalemia and nephrotoxicity. This recommendation is based on moderate-quality evidence. 9. Immediate initiation of antiretroviral therapy (ART) is not recommended in HIV-infected patients with cryptococcal meningitis due to the high risk of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS), which can be life-threatening. ART initiation should be deferred until there is evidence of sustained clinical response to antifungal therapy, typically after 4 weeks of induction and consolidation treatment with Amphotericin B-containing regimens combined with flucytosine or fluconazole, or after 4–6 weeks of high-dose oral fluconazole induction and consolidation therapy. This is a conditional recommendation based on low-quality evidence. 10. Discontinuation of azole maintenance therapy (secondary prophylaxis) in HIV-infected adults and adolescents with successfully treated cryptococcal disease is recommended under specific criteria. If HIV viral load monitoring is available, patients should be stable and adherent to ART and antifungal maintenance therapy for at least one year, with a CD4 cell count ≥200 cells/mm³ (two measurements 6 months apart). This is a strong recommendation based on low-quality evidence. 11. In children under 2 years of age with successfully treated cryptococcal disease, antifungal maintenance therapy should not be discontinued. This is a strong recommendation based on low-quality evidence. 12. In children aged 2–5 years with successfully treated cryptococcal disease, discontinuation of antifungal maintenance therapy is recommended if the child is stable and adherent to ART and antifungal maintenance therapy for at least one year, with a CD4 cell count percentage >25% or an absolute count >750 cells/mm³ (two measurements 6 months apart). This is a strong recommendation based on low-quality evidence. 13. Maintenance therapy for cryptococcal disease should be restarted if the CD4 count drops to ≤100 cells/mm³ in HIV-infected adults and adolescents, or ≤25% or 750 cells/mm³ in children aged 2–5 years, or if a WHO stage 4 clinical event occurs, regardless of patient age. This is a strong recommendation based on low-quality evidence. 14. Cardiovascular risk assessment and management should be provided for all individuals living with HIV according to standard protocols recommended for the general population. This is a conditional recommendation based on very low-quality evidence. 15. Depression assessment and management should be included in the package of HIV care services for all individuals living with HIV. This is a conditional recommendation based on very low-quality evidence. 16. Following an HIV diagnosis, a package of support interventions should be offered to ensure timely linkage to care for all people living with HIV. This is a strong recommendation based on moderate-quality evidence. 17. Less frequent clinical visits (every 3–6 months) are recommended for people stable on ART. This is a strong recommendation based on moderate-quality evidence. 18. Less frequent medication pickups (every 3–6 months) are recommended for people stable on ART. This is a strong recommendation based on low-quality evidence. 19. Decentralization of HIV treatment and care should be considered to increase access and improve retention in care. This includes initiating ART in hospitals with maintenance at peripheral health facilities, or initiating and maintaining ART at peripheral health facilities or community levels. These are strong recommendations based on lowto moderate-quality evidence. 20. ART should be initiated and maintained in eligible pregnant and postpartum women and infants at maternal and child healthcare settings, with linkage to ongoing HIV care and ART where appropriate. This is a strong recommendation based on very low-quality evidence. 21. ART should be initiated and maintained in eligible people living with HIV at care settings where opioid substitution therapy (OST) is provided. This is a strong recommendation based on very low-quality evidence. 22. Adolescent-friendly health services should be implemented in HIV services to ensure engagement and improved outcomes. This is a strong recommendation based on low-quality evidence. 23. Adolescents should be counseled about the potential benefits and risks of disclosing their HIV status to others and supported in determining if, when, how, and to whom to disclose. This is a conditional recommendation based on very low-quality evidence.
